title: The Burnt Border
premise: Vesper Fairweather, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths in row twelve of Flight 4471, is pulled into a debt they never incurred when a stranger named Ilse arrives claiming Vesper once saved her life—and that the favor must now be repaid by hiding a whistleblower's data. The data exposes a cartel of arms brokers and government insiders who downed Flight 4471 to silence a witness, meaning Vesper's family was collateral in a transaction. Racing from a safehouse in Trieste to Frankfurt before markets open, Vesper and Ilse must outrun an assassin named Corvus and get the truth past three governments that each want it buried. Vesper survives by choosing exposure over invisibility, testifying as the markets crash, and finally sleeping through the night—grieving, but belonging to the living again.
about_author: Juniper Underhill is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading the quiet arithmetic of disaster before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse near the Baltic coast, where the fog arrives on schedule and nothing is ever on fire.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Insomnia-ridden Vesper works crash sites for a living, cataloging other people's worst days, and revisits the reconstructed cabin of Flight 4471 one more time. A routine debris report contains a serial number that shouldn't exist—filed twice, in two countries. Emotional beat: grief calcified into procedure, cracked by the first anomaly.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ilse arrives at Vesper's apartment claiming Vesper pulled her from a burning car in Trieste—a night Vesper has no memory of—and leaves a sealed drive as 'interest owed.' Within hours, Vesper's security clearances are revoked and a man with a leather glove is asking neighbors questions. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a life being rewritten around you.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse explains the debt economy she operates in: favors as currency, debts as chains. The drive holds testimony from a dead whistleblower about Meridian Group, a brokerage that moves weapons through three governments' blind spots. Vesper refuses; then Corvus burns the apartment. Emotional beat: refusal curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Trieste Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing to Trieste, Vesper and Ilse trace the phantom favor to its source: Vesper's own father, a customs officer, who once hid Ilse's mother—and whose signature appears in Meridian's ledger beside Flight 4471's cargo manifest. Emotional beat: the discovery that family history is entangled with the crime.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper uses investigator credentials to approach an honest-seeming EU aviation auditor, who reveals the downing was authorized as a 'containment event'—then betrays them with a single phone call. Corvus nearly takes them at the train station. Emotional beat: trust as a weapon turned against you.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV, first and only time. The assassin's methodical chapter: he studies Vesper's file, notes the insomnia, the row twelve obsession, and decides the cleanest kill is psychological. He sends Vesper a photograph of the cockpit's last seconds. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy—the hunter who understands the hunted better than anyone.

chapters.title: The Night Market
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Hiding in Frankfurt's underbelly, Ilse trades a decade of accumulated favors to buy one hour of safe passage and a journalist's encrypted line. She confesses the truth: there was no burning car; her debt is to Vesper's father, and she chose Vesper because grief makes people brave. Emotional beat: betrayal confessed, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dawn in Frankfurt. Meridian's lawyers move to suppress; two governments deny everything; the third offers Vesper money and silence. With ninety minutes to market open, Vesper and Ilse split—the drive to the journalist, Vesper as visible decoy through the exchange's lobby. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Climax. Vesper's POV. Corvus corners Vesper in the exchange's atrium but hesitates—Vesper names the flight, the row, the manifest, making the kill a public event he can't contain. The data goes live; Meridian's stock freefalls; the auditor's recording surfaces. Corvus walks away, debt unfulfilled. Emotional beat: survival by refusing to be invisible.

chapters.title: What the Living Owe
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, months later. Testimony given, three governments scandalized, Vesper rebuilds the row twelve memorial with the real passenger list—names the cover-up had shuffled. Ilse leaves a train ticket, not an apology; Vesper buys a second one. Final image: Vesper asleep until morning, for the first time in years. Emotional beat: grief integrated, belonging chosen.
